name: QAR overall: QS1's sub-metrics weighted by its ideals, with floor and ceiling
purpose: Measures how far QAR as a whole is from its ideals by combining the sub-metrics QME1 to QME7, each normalised to the range zero to one by a stated rule (pass rate; pass rate scaled by cost per passing turn; the share of solutions whose selection follows a current row) and weighted by the ideals of QS1: a weight per ideal with its reason in esoi.toml [balance.metric-qar-overall], split equally over the sub-metrics that serve it. Each sub-metric has a cheap tier (offline arms, or a small sampled run of a paid arm) for the everyday QUICK score and a full tier (the whole input set, against a live model where the arm is paid, run only by decision with a budget) for the FULL score. It is computed from recorded rows only and never re-runs an arm; an arm whose row is stale, missing or not built is unmeasured and never counted as a pass.
record: Per tier: the headline (the weighted value over the measured weight only), the floor (unmeasured counted as zero), the ceiling (unmeasured counted as one) and the measured share of the weight; per sub-metric its value, tier, and the date, commit and cost of each arm's last row; and what is not measured, with the command and estimated cost that would measure it, all printed by the command. The results row counts the sub-metrics measured on current rows and at or above the bar in esoi.toml. Re-run it after any results change: it costs nothing.

name: Exactly-once mid-run delivery per run, and how fast it is seen
purpose: synthetic cases: a message pushed before or during a run reaches the next planner decision once, only for its own conversation, and is never silently lost (through a real Orchestrator), plus the inbox port contract. For a deep worker with a live session, offline against a scripted stand-in for Claude Code: each message is written once and only to its own run (two concurrent runs never cross), a message landing as the run finishes is delivered once or left unclaimed, a message written but not confirmed seen is handed back as unseen, an ignored interrupt ends in terminate then kill, and work finished before a stop or pause is present when the session resumes. Measured on top, with real runs: send-to-seen latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time and cost per run Read in this direction: cut the time from send to seen. A distributed inbox (for example Redis) is a consumer's and is not compared, and the loop cases cover the planner's drain points only. The live deep-worker session is pinned offline against a scripted stand-in, which cannot show latency, acted-on share, stop-to-quiet time or cost; the task and chat surfaces still claim through a 15 s throttle outside a live session.

The one-shot arm scores its latency as the end of the run by construction.

name: Example runnability on an empty environment
purpose: offline cases over the example scripts and qar.toml: compile, import, run to its help or not-configured exit in a scrubbed environment, the stub provider, README coverage, secret and machine-path scan; zero model calls e2e_demo.py and textual_demo.py need a live Quest backend and a terminal, so only their import, refusal-to-start and stub behaviour are scored, not a full run.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Task lifecycle correctness over offline cases
purpose: offline cases: poll, claim, run and report lifecycle (done, failed, needs-you with a decision, duplicate scan, lost claim, scheduled-not-yet-due, team scoping, unconfigured), persona selection by exact structured field, quest-folder pull and push (idempotent, human text kept, bullets pushed once), folder ownership, local-time scheduling, env-file and flag handling; fake Quest client and scripted model only, zero model calls The edge is a fake Quest client and a scripted model, so wire-level behaviour (HTTP errors, real Quest payload shapes) is not scored; the quest_client tests and the dev-Quest qualitative run pin it.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Configuration precedence and validation correctness
purpose: offline cases: file fields and the [personas] table, loud rejection of unknown, adapter-only and malformed keys, env beats file, process beats env_files beats env table, earlier env file wins, alias outranks a shared file, blank placeholders do not block defaults, tuning values (bad value falls back to default, zero turns deep review off); zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise correct precedence across file, environment and process sources; maximise the share of typos, unsupported keys and malformed values that are rejected or defaulted as specified; keep model calls at zero. Covers the scalar fields a lane commonly sets, not every one of the roughly 100 RunnerConfig fields.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Command-line parsing, refusal and output correctness
purpose: offline cases through the real cli main() and tools main(): --help for every subcommand, unknown command and flag, missing and malformed arguments, write methods refused without --write, no-credentials messages, the context store commands on a scratch folder, and the tool catalog list, show and call with a custom tool; zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise the share of subcommands that parse and print what a person needs to act; maximise bad invocations refused with the usage exit code before any action; keep model calls at zero. The interactive surfaces (chat TUI, poll loop, channel, serve-files) need a terminal or a server and are pinned only by their own tests.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Model tier selection and limit-recognition correctness
purpose: offline cases: deep starting rung per difficulty and ladder (synonyms, unknown rating, off-ladder start, operator mapping), family resolution to the newest live id, tier resolution with and without live models and pins, lower-tier fallback, vision capability, outage wording, usage-limit detection and reset parsing; zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise the share of work started on the cheapest adequate rung; maximise correct resolution of names to live models with operator pins always winning; maximise correct recognition of outages and allowance limits and of their reset time. Measures that the right model is chosen, not that it was the cheapest one that still succeeded, which needs live runs.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Cost, budget and resource-guard correctness
purpose: offline cases: price per provider and model (including unknown model and provider), bootstrap cost estimate, provider detection from the environment, daily budget (limit, off, bad value, negative tokens, restart reload), and resource-guard hysteresis for memory, free memory and load; zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise correctness of per-model price lookup with a stated default for unknown models; maximise budget accuracy across restarts and day boundaries; minimise flapping of the host guard by using hysteresis. Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices (input tokens only), so a provider price change is not noticed until the table is edited.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

purpose: Collection proves tests import and parametrise, not that they pass or stay offline; a missing fixture only fails at setup.

name: Secret detection and placeholder tolerance
purpose: offline cases: planted secrets assembled from fragments (keys, tokens, private key block, home paths, object id, address), documented placeholders that must stay quiet, the repository clean in file groups, command runs in a throwaway git repo; zero model calls Read in this direction: maximise detection of every known secret kind planted in text; minimise false findings on documented placeholders; keep the repository itself scanning clean. The scan reads working files unless `esoi hygiene --history` is asked for, and knows only the secret shapes in the esoi hygiene scanner, so a vendor token with a new shape passes until the scanner gains a pattern and a planted case is added.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

purpose: A typo in [selections] for run-deep-work does not raise: resolve_deep_runner degrades to no deep runner (SEL-034 pins it). Only three live call sites are driven.

name: Documentation coverage and voice conformance
purpose: offline cases generated from the repo by generate_cases.py: relative links and em dashes per document, index coverage, docs named by each component row, a described row per environment variable, each CLI subcommand and public name documented, and a coverage case that fails when a document or variable has no case; zero model calls Read in this direction: minimise broken links and orphan documents; maximise coverage of every environment variable, subcommand and public name; eliminate disallowed punctuation from documents. Some documents still contain em dashes, against the house voice rule; the failing cases name each one.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Prediction store contract pass rate
purpose: share of persistence contract scenarios (roundtrip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart, tolerance) the store passes; a share held out Read in this direction: maximise exact round trip of saved data; maximise scope isolation; maximise correct expiry; maximise survival across a restart; ensure no store call raises. Backends differ in where data lives, not in how well they store it. Prediction quality is not measured at all: no case set replays recorded ask sequences through the anticipation engine, so nothing says how often a served prediction is right or what a wrong one costs.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Autopilot gate decision correctness
purpose: labelled gate cases (budget, cadence in the quest zone, Run now, reactive, roster day, backpressure) run through the production AutopilotPass for one quest with a scripted Quest client and a pinned clock, a share held out, zero model calls; a baseline with elapsed-time cadence and no roster fails them Read in this direction: maximise correct run and skip decisions against the person's settings; eliminate runs past the daily budget or on a day nobody was rostered; minimise spend before the decision. Only the decision to run is scored. What a pass writes once it runs is unmeasured beyond size (assemble-a-prompt), and whether the moment suits the person is not scored, only that their settings are followed.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of the live implementation on the rule's cases, recorded as a row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash; a rule holds or does not, so the implementations are never ranked and a deliberately broken baseline must fail the same cases.

name: Parts selected by measurement
purpose: share of solutions whose selected implementation has a recorded result on the committed code and is not beaten by a rival on the same cases
record: share of solutions whose selected implementation has a recorded result on the committed code and is not beaten by a rival on the same cases, from esoi check --strict

name: Intent-grounded pass rate
purpose: Share of cases whose reply meets the case rubric where the right answer depends on the person's intent (which quest to focus on, a request that conflicts with an ideal, a gap under an intent, a plan that cannot reach its vision, which experiment to run); hard checks by code first (names the gap or ideal by its exact text, invents no quest, no em dash), then the existing chat-quality judge on the cheapest tier; a no-intent control that must be unchanged Read in this direction: raise the intent-grounded pass rate.
record: The pass rate of each arm on the same cases, with input tokens per passing case as the tie-break, as rows of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash. The intent_grounding cases are not built yet; the arms are run by decision under the metric run policy.

name: First-pass acceptance and exploration before the first edit
purpose: Share of replayed tasks the done verifier accepts on the first attempt, the mean read and search calls before the first edit on the second task for the same solution, and the count of new files outside the records and the code (which must be none) Read in this direction: raise the share of tasks accepted on the first attempt; lower the exploration before the first edit on a repeat task for the same solution.
record: Each arm on the same replayed tasks, recorded as rows pinned to the commit and the cases hash. The task_replay cases are not built yet; the arms are run by decision under the metric run policy.

name: Accuracy of core ML tasks over labelled cases
purpose: How often each alternative classifies a quest or input correctly, or recommends something a person accepts, on held-out labelled cases. Read in this direction: maximise correct classifications and useful recommendations on held-out labelled cases from real Quest data; minimise cost per correct answer and the number of separate classifiers that do the same job. Only the message router alternatives and the registry-conditioned intent routing have recorded runs; which-quest classification, area-of-life classification and the three recommenders have no labelled case set, and the two which-quest rankers do the same job on separate paths.
record: Accuracy of each implementation on the same cases, with cost per correct answer as the tie-break.

name: Specification selection pass rate
purpose: Measures whether a request is answered with the records it concerns (and with nothing when no record concerns it) without returning a crowd, over the real index of the ESOI repository's records, with a real cheap-model judge and a real local vector search.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same labelled requests (every expected id present, no more than a ceiling returned), per kind, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash. Every model call is a real one, so a run costs real tokens and the pass rate moves a little between runs. The scripted-judge plumbing checks (batching, invented ids, failed calls) are unit tests, not this metric. The leaderboard ranks the arms by a balanced score of accuracy, cost and time, weighted in esoi.toml [balance.spec_selection].
command: esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector_gated; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector_llm; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_only

name: Cards per source-file group after repeated passes, for the guards that prevent growth
purpose: Measures, offline, whether a card store stays at one card per distinct topic of its source files as the runner builds and opens it. The card_store_growth arm builds stores through repeated passes with the library's guards and the runner's shipped settings: nested stores, a legacy store opened as a runner opens it, and the card limit. The card_growth component's fixture stores are inflated the way copy mode inflated real ones (two stores, one nested in the other's corpus, copying each other's current cards for a stated number of bootstrap passes, plus a taught card and a managed card, and in some cases two bootstrap cards for one topic pinning the same file, a card a person wrote with no provenance, a note a run added to a compounded copy, and two distinct topics of one file); its bootstrap_guards arm opens them as the runner does, so that score includes the runner's tidy at open. A group is the files a card pins together with its topic name. Read in this direction: lower cards per group toward one and the duplicate share toward none, with no group lost and nothing a person or a run wrote lost.
record: Per case: cards before and after, distinct groups, cards per group, duplicate share, groups lost, whether the cards that must be left alone remain and whether a run's note is still held; a card_growth case passes with one card per group, no group lost, every protected card kept and the note kept; a card_store_growth case passes when its stated invariant holds after the passes. One row per arm per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call. The broken baseline is run by hand (esoi run card_growth --impl card_growth.broken.drop_every_import:build) because a metric command names arms under impls/ only.
command: esoi run card_growth --impl bootstrap_guards; esoi run card_store_growth --impl live_store; esoi run card_growth --impl no_cleanup

name: Cards per source-file group and duplicate share after a repair of an inflated store
purpose: Measures, offline, whether a repair brings a card store that already inflated back to one card per distinct topic of its source files without losing what a person or a run wrote, on the card_growth fixture stores (inflated the way copy mode inflated real ones, with a taught card, a managed card, a card a person wrote with no provenance, a note a run added to a compounded copy and two distinct topics of one file). The repository_tidy arm loads each store into a backend-shaped repository in memory and applies the tidy as a lane with card_tidy = apply does; the quarantine_tool arm runs the script with --apply; the no_cleanup arm is the floor. The local-folder tidy at open has no arm of its own and is read through the bootstrap_guards arm of card_growth. Read in this direction: lower cards per group toward one and the duplicate share toward none, with no group lost and nothing a person or a run wrote lost.
record: Per case: cards before and after, distinct groups, cards per group, duplicate share, groups lost, whether the cards a repair must leave alone remain and whether a run's note is still held; a case passes with one card per group, no group lost, every protected card kept and the note kept. One row per arm per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call.
command: esoi run card_growth --impl repository_tidy; esoi run card_growth --impl quarantine_tool; esoi run card_growth --impl no_cleanup

name: Mixed card and specification selection, with both existing selection metrics held
purpose: Measures whether one search puts the right cards and the right records in view together. Runs on a combined labelled set of requests and on the existing context_selection and spec_selection cases as its two halves, so a merged pipeline is compared with the two separate ones on the same cases. The combined set is evaluation/components/context_and_specs (generic fixture cards beside the spec_selection fixture index, with a problem and an intent that no solution serves and a fixture tag), with three kinds of request: ones whose right answer mixes a source (a file, a note, a conversation) and the solution, problem or metric it served; ones whose best match is a problem or an intent with no solution yet, labelled with that record and "no solution yet"; and ones that match only an ideal or a metric, labelled with the record a link should bring. The mixed set also holds a card alone, a solution alone, a runbook, a file with a failing metric, paraphrases, a past conversation, a change named by a tag (R3), two overlapping solutions (R1), an unrelated request, a note with its problem and an implementation's name; an ambiguous request is live only. The offline arms call no model. The merged arm runs on the two halves as esoi run spec_selection --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links and esoi run context_selection --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links, free arms only, compared with the best free arm already recorded there (lexical_vector and hybrid_union or idf_docstrings); the gated paid spec arm is not re-run for it.
record: Per arm on the same cases: the mixed-case pass rate (every expected card and record present, no more than the ceiling returned, the "no solution yet" mark where expected), the spec_selection balanced score and the context_selection pass rate on their own cases, and model calls per assembly; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. An arm that drops either existing metric does not win.
command: esoi run context_and_specs --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links; esoi run spec_selection --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links; esoi run context_selection --impl solutions_and_problems_with_links

name: Runs that leave a durable, attributed record of what they changed
purpose: Measures, over replayed or recorded runs, the share whose before and after reading is durably attached to the solution it served, the share that state what they moved, the share of runs that showed a record wrong or missing and fixed it in the same change with what changed and why on the record, and the files created per run, which must be none. A change the AI makes to a record counts only when it is made, not when it is proposed; a proposal counts only for the owner's own words (an intent's vision statement, the ideals the owner wrote), which the AI does not edit. Read in this direction: raise the three shares, keep new files at none. A milestone metric of iterate-by-spec, whose authoritative metric is metric-iterate-by-spec.
record: Each arm on the same runs, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash.

name: Right solution missed without the tag
purpose: Measures whether the tags identify the solutions a change must consult, in two parts. Recorded now, offline: the mechanical half of the first milestone, on fixture tag files (evaluation/components/tag_solutions): the rule passes a good file and fails each fault a person can make without judgement (a tag with no problem link, with no meaning, on every solution, used by none, linking a problem id that is not a record, a tag outside the list, a problem id copied into the tags column), and the lookup finds a solution through its tags and through its connected problems.
record: Offline part: per case, the rule's problem lines and notes against the faults the case names, or the solutions the lookup returns; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call, and the deliberately broken baseline (esoi run tag_solutions --impl tag_solutions.broken.membership_only:build, run by hand because a metric command names arms under impls/ only) must fail. Planned part: per tag, the share of labelled requests where the right solution is missed without it, against the share with all tags.
disadvantages: Planned and unmeasured until search-cards-and-specs and its labelled requests exist: whether each tag mitigates the problems it links, as the share of labelled requests where a solution that covers or constrains the change is missed with the tags and with each tag removed in turn; a tag whose removal misses nothing more is retired.

name: Copies kept out with real material kept in, by review availability
purpose: Measures, offline, what a lane takes in when its corpus root sits above a backups folder of dated snapshots, each carrying a card store and a copy of the corpus's nested store, beside one legitimate nested store and an ordinary docs folder. The solution is installed at the gate seam the bootstrap and the walk ask, and the library's real bootstrap runs in copy mode and in mount mode, with the folder review unavailable (no provider), switched off, failing on every call, answering skip for the snapshots, or answering index for everything; plus a corpus over the review's file-count floor, a person's index verdict in folder_review.json, a pair of snapshots, and a lone snapshot (kept as a known gap). The review's answers are fixed per case, so what is measured is how each implementation acts on each verdict, not whether a model judges a folder rightly. Read in this direction: series cards, mounts and open snapshot folders toward none where they should be kept out, with nothing real lost and no index verdict overruled.
record: Per case: cards imported or stores mounted from the series, snapshot folders the walk may enter, whether the nested store was taken in, whether the docs folder stayed indexed, and the folder review calls answered; a case passes when the series is kept out (or, under an index verdict, let in) and the nested store and docs are kept. One row per arm in the results log pinned to the commit and the cases hash, with no model call; the index-everything baseline is run by hand (esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl choose_what_to_index.broken.index_everything:build) because a metric command names arms under impls/ only.
command: esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl risk_gate; esoi run choose_what_to_index --impl review_only

name: Step continuity at cost over multi-step requests
purpose: Measures whether every step of a multi-step request acts consistently with what the request established earlier (a refusal, a correction, the resolved request, an earlier finding), at a cost the fast tier can carry. Read in this direction: maximise requests whose every step is consistent; hold the chat judge pass rate; minimise input tokens per request, counting cached tokens apart. Its cases include requests a coding agent completes, so the share the chat completes beside it is read too.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled multi-step requests: the share of requests with no inconsistent step, the chat judge pass rate, and uncached and cached input tokens per request; and the share of the coding agent's completed requests the implementation also completes; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Scripted requests are shorter than real sessions, so a failure that needs a long one may not show; cache behaviour differs by vendor and may not show offline; it cannot tell whether an item should have been admitted, which the admission metric judges.

name: Goal-relevant admission at a precision floor with nothing out of scope
purpose: Measures whether the items admitted to the working stream are the ones the request's goal needs. Read in this direction: maximise needed items admitted at or above a precision floor; admit no out-of-scope item; minimise model calls per step.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled steps: recall of needed items at the precision floor, near misses admitted, out-of-scope items admitted, and model calls per step; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. The labels of needed and near miss are the case author's judgment; items are judged one step at a time, so it cannot see whether the final answer improved.

name: Supported and calibrated answers to world questions
purpose: Measures whether claims about the world are supported by a cited source and stated with a confidence that matches the evidence. Read in this direction: maximise supported claims; minimise the gap between stated confidence and how often claims hold; minimise cost per answer.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled world questions: the share of claims supported by a cited source, a calibration error over stated confidence, and cost per answer; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Reference evidence strength is set by the case author; a supported claim can still be the wrong advice for the person; a live research source makes runs differ over time.

name: Combined world score: goals met, honest reach and receipts, cost, time, context efficiency and safety
purpose: Measures which configuration should do the AI's work in the world, combining several things into one score. Read in this direction: maximise outside goals whose done-standard is verified as met; maximise capability and blocker claims that match the inventory and claimed acts that have a receipt; minimise cost per goal, counting cached tokens apart; minimise wall time; minimise tokens spent finding context before the first change; allow no write outside the boundary and no cross-scope read. Each factor is normalised and weighted by the solution's ideals, with floors for safety and honest claims, so a cheap configuration that writes out of bounds or claims work it did not do cannot win. Its cases include people with no external environment, whose reach is in-app operations, documentation and the web.
record: Per implementation on the same cases: share of goals met, share of claims matching the inventory, share of claimed acts with a receipt, cost and tokens per goal, wall time, context tokens before the first change, boundary and scope violations, and the combined score with its weights; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm, command or weights exist yet; the weights are for the specification owner to set. Real goals take minutes and cost money, so the set must be small and runs are paid by decision; a combined score can hide one bad factor behind good ones, which the floors only partly prevent; it assumes the inventory is right; it cannot see quality a verifier misses.

name: Account-state consistency across scripted sessions
purpose: Measures whether what the AI says about the person's account is true when said and consistent across a session. Read in this direction: maximise state claims that match the store at reply time; allow no contradiction and no repeated or re-proposed change; minimise reads per turn. Its cases include questions about how to use the app, answered from the product documentation, and claims about what the AI can do in the app.
record: Per implementation on the same scripted sessions: the share of state claims matching the store at reply time, contradictions per session, repeated or re-proposed changes, and reads per turn; and the share of app-usage questions answered correctly and in-app capability claims that are true; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. It needs a disposable host account and the host's real operations, so it cannot run wholly offline; it sees only changes the script makes, not concurrent ones; a claim extractor decides what counts as a state claim.

name: Representative long-view carry-through across assigned quests, with nothing outside its branch
purpose: Measures whether each request a representative handles starts from what its assigned quests and their intents have already settled, and whether that stays inside the representative's branch. Read in this direction: maximise multi-session cases passed (a decline on one assigned quest holds on another, a correction applies, chat and background work agree, no question asked again once declined); allow no item to reach another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person; add no time before the reply.
record: Per implementation on the same multi-session cases: the share passed, items reaching another representative's quests, a sibling intent or another person, time added before the reply, and model calls per request; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet, and the hierarchy-aware fence it counts against does not exist in the library. Scripted sessions are far shorter than months of use; a pass can come from the current message rather than the long view; a wrong line in a maintained view that no case asks about is invisible; hierarchies in the cases are the author's, and a real person's may be deeper. The host's existing live checks (a declined proposal not re-proposed, retrieval scoped to the active quest) can seed the cases.

name: Requests held to their ESOI metric by code
purpose: Measures whether the rule that every request applies its relevant ESOI metric holds in the flow, by code. Read in this direction: maximise the share of requests with an applicable metric that were measured before and after by code and did not regress, or whose regression was answered; maximise the share of metric-less requests for which a metric was proposed; allow no regression left without a response; add no time before a chat reply. Every count comes from the runner's ledger and records, never from a model's text.
record: Per implementation on the same replayed requests across chat turns, queued tasks and deep runs: the share measured and not regressed, the share of metric-less requests with a proposed metric, regressions left unanswered, time added before the reply, and model calls per request; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. The same shares can be read from a live lane's ledger.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. It sees that a metric was applied, not that it was the right metric or the right slice, so a weak metric applied everywhere scores well; a proposed metric may be poor and is counted the same as a good one; a recorded row the worker wrote counts less than a measured one only if the arm says so; whether the person's own quest metric later moved takes weeks and is outside it.

name: Representative choice accuracy and thread consistency
purpose: Measures whether each request is handled by the representative that fits it and whether a thread keeps one representative. Read in this direction: maximise requests whose chosen representative matches the label; maximise spawned work that keeps its thread's representative; allow no selection by a bare mention or of a representative the person cannot see; minimise questions to the person and model calls.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled requests: the share matching the label, the share of spawned work keeping its thread's representative, selections by bare mention or of a hidden representative, questions asked, and model calls per choice; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. The label of the right representative is the case author's judgment of fit; it cannot see whether the person would have preferred another; the host's chat classifier runs in the host, so its arm needs the host.

name: Supported first beats within the time and cost the turn allows
purpose: offline cases of a turn's events with the beat a model wrote: maximise the share of beats whose every claim is backed by an event of the turn (value), under a first-beat time that does not delay the answer (time) and a cost per beat below the cost of the answer it precedes (cost); a beat that is refused, empty or unsupported counts against it, and a turn with narration off costs nothing. Reads the narration call only; which events exist is show-progress.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Support is judged against the event list, not against whether the person found the beat useful; a bland beat is always supported, so a length or specificity floor is needed in the cases.

name: Faithful explanations per unit of cost and time
purpose: offline cases of a turn's trace with the explanation a model wrote: maximise the share of explanations whose every step is in the trace and which omit no step that changed the answer (value), at a cost per explanation below a stated share of the turn's cost and with no time added before the reply. Reads the explanation call only; explain-qar checks the documentation, not this.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Faithfulness is judged against the trace the runner kept, so a trace that omits a step makes a fabricated step look unsupported only when the cases hold it; whether people read the explanation is not measured.

name: Answer pass rate gained per image described
purpose: offline cases of image-bearing requests answered with and without the description: maximise the pass-rate gain the description gives on those cases (value), at a cost per image below the cost of the answer it informs and a description time that does not hold the turn longer than the person would wait; an image whose description changes no verdict is cost without value and counts against it.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no image cases, arm or command exist yet, and a live arm needs a vision model call, so it runs only by decision. Pass rate depends on the answering model as much as on the description.

name: Hand-offs a person keeps per unit of cost and time
purpose: from the goals the judge handled: maximise the share of its verdicts that a person did not reassign or reverse (value), at a cost per goal below the cost of the reassignment it avoids and a verdict time inside goal creation that the person does not notice. Counted from the host's reassignment records, never from the model's words; a lane that keeps no such record cannot read it.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set or arm exists yet. Reassignment is a late and noisy signal, a person may keep a wrong verdict, and a goal that is never reassigned looks right.

name: Drafted metrics accepted per unit of cost
purpose: from drafts offered to owners: maximise the share of drafted metrics the owner accepts without rewriting their rule (value), at a cost per accepted draft below the cost of the owner writing one and within the call cap the module states (cost), with drafting off the reply path (time). Counted from the owner's accept or edit, never from the draft's own claim.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set or arm exists yet. Acceptance can reflect fatigue as much as quality, and an accepted metric may still be a poor one; whether the metric later moved is outside it.

name: Retrieval hits and category precision per unit of cost
purpose: offline cases of cards and labelled files: maximise the card retrieval hit rate with the metadata against without it and the share of files placed in their labelled card (value), at a cost per card or file below the cost of the retrieval misses it removes (cost), run only on creation or refresh so no reply waits on it (time). A label that changes no retrieval or placement result is cost without value.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set or arm exists yet. Labelled placement cases are small and written by hand; a live arm needs model calls and runs only by decision.

name: Correct terminal helper verdicts within the wait a person accepts
purpose: offline cases of labelled terminal commands and asks: maximise the share classified and judged as labelled (value), at a latency per command that a person at a prompt does not notice (time) and a cost per command below the cost of a wrong route; a helper call whose verdict a rule could give is cost without value, and an acknowledgement that adds latency without information counts against it.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set or arm exists yet. Labelled commands are few; the acknowledgement's usefulness to a person is a judgement the cases cannot make, so removing the call is an open option.

name: Justified share of model spend
purpose: share of AVERAGE model spend on prompts that are registered, whose owner metric has a current row on production-shaped cases, and whose call beats its ablation on average while its MAXIMUM cost, tokens and latency stay within that prompt's own budget (bar 0.8). Kept per prompt: fire rate per turn, tokens in and out, dollars per call, latency and whether it is on the critical path, each as average and maximum; budgets set per prompt from the value its owner metric shows. Stats come from the per-call usage records tagged with the spec id and from production-shaped eval cases; until production data exists rows come from eval traces and are labelled so.
record: Per prompt and in total, with the commit and the cases hash; one row per run. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no ablation arm, command or row exists, and spend-weighted value is not computed. Rows from eval traces are not production data and are labelled so; a budget set from a weak owner metric inherits its weakness.

name: Justified model spend
purpose: share of average model spend that is justified: registered, measured by its owner metric, better than its ablation and inside its own budget
record: share of average model spend that is justified: registered, measured by its owner metric, better than its ablation and inside its own budget. Read from metric-justified-model-spend; NOT BUILT, so it keeps its weight unmeasured.

name: Whole-path turns right on a small mixed set
purpose: a dozen labelled messages spread over the kinds of request QAR serves (a question about the person's own data, an absent fact, a note, a goal, a conditional multi-step ask, an unpinned quest named only by its content, a web question, a queued hand-off, a terminal request, a request it cannot do, a bulk delete that needs a yes): maximise the share of turns that are right end to end (route, context, plan, act, answer) by the world afterwards and the reply, at a cost in model calls and time per turn that a person accepts, with no write nobody asked for.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with model calls and seconds per turn and the pass rate by kind; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. Unconfirmed: proposed 2026-10-29 so that the whole path has one measure; the label set is small and rewritten from existing sources.
disadvantages: A dozen cases rank no two implementations that differ by a case or two, and one run of a live model varies between runs. The world is a small placeholder account behind the real tool catalogue, not a real Quest, so a failure may be the world's gap and must be read before it is called a defect. The scripted arm shows what the code around a model does for a model that is exactly right, not how a model decides.

name: Two-sided long-term guidance: grounded nudges at the right level, restraint elsewhere
purpose: Measures whether a reply points the person at the real next milestone and the real current reading at a natural moment, at the intent level that fits (goal, quest, or a representative's portfolio), after answering the request and briefly; and whether it holds back when the moment is wrong. Read in this direction: maximise nudge cases right and restraint cases right together (the value is their mean); allow no invented milestone or figure; allow no pointer in an urgent, narrow, unrelated, emotional or repeated case.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled cases: nudge cases right, restraint cases right, awkwardness on restraint cases, each per intent level (quest, goal, rep), and model calls per case, the grader's included; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash.
disadvantages: Twenty-four invented scenarios, so a first reading, not a population; the right level and the right moment are the case author's judgment; the grader is a model (sonnet through claude -p) and the reply model is the cheap tier, so the figures move with both.

name: Hub of hubs: coverage, integration by configuration, research freshness, code structure
purpose: Measures, offline, how far QAR is a hub of hubs. Per area of esoi/hubs.csv seven checks hold or not: a hub is registered or none is recorded as existing, at least half the capabilities arrive by configuration, research is within 90 days, the area has one seam in code, its hub is selectable by metric, core holds no vendor branch for it, and a fake hub added through its configuration entry works with zero library edits. Read in this direction: coverage, integration by configuration and freshness up, vendor branches down.
record: Per area and check pass or fail with the reason; coverage; the share of capabilities needing no code per integration; days since research per area (oldest and mean); the vendor branches found in core with file and line; the combined score; one row per run pinned to the commit and cases hash, no model call. The floor is run by hand (esoi run hub_of_hubs --impl hub_of_hubs.broken.vendor_grep:build).
disadvantages: Freshness is the date a person or the autopilot recorded, not proof that the research was good; findings are from secondary web results; a probe exists for four of ten areas; the capability list is hand-kept.

name: Hub of hubs
purpose: share of the hub-of-hubs checks that hold: hubs registered, built on by configuration, researched within 90 days, one seam per area, no vendor branch in core, a fake hub accepted by configuration
record: share of the hub-of-hubs checks that hold: hubs registered, built on by configuration, researched within 90 days, one seam per area, no vendor branch in core, a fake hub accepted by configuration. Read from metric-hub-of-hubs; offline.
